headline: Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki out 2-4 weeks with upper-body injury
take:
Per ESPN, Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki is out two to four weeks with an upper-body injury. The Athletic reports that Suzuki, hit by a shot against the Sharks on Tuesday, will see his ironman streak of 546 games, the second-longest active streak in the NHL, end Friday.

The timing hurts. So far this season, Suzuki has 12 points in nine games and 5 goals, about one more than the quality of his chances would predict (his own expected goals, a measure of shot quality, are 3.94). At 5-on-5, MTL controls 56.92% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share rises 5.66 points when he plays. MTL is 4-3-2, and its overall expected goals share is 49.2%, so he is propping up a team that is otherwise roughly even. His 21.78 minutes a night and first power-play role will be hard to replace.

Going by how the coach has used his players, Cole Caufield (19:26 a night) is next in line for Suzuki's even-strength minutes. Oliver Kapanen, the busiest man on the second power-play unit, is the likeliest to move up to the top unit.
